method: Independent refutation pass over sections 3, 4 and 5 by a BM (Malaysia) editor. Every external claim cites a URL fetched on 2026-09-07: DBP PRPM Kamus Dewan entries, the DBP Khidmat Nasihat archive (prpmv1.dbp.gov.my), DBP Istilah rows, HRD Corp BM pages, the MQA BM FAQ, the Ministry of National Unity circular KPN.BKP.PA.100-1/7/1 of 14 Februari 2022 on letters, memos and e-mail, Surat Pekeliling Am Bil. 4 Tahun 2014 (Jabatan Perdana Menteri, honorifics), Jobstreet Malaysia's surat rasmi and e-mel guides, and a Munsyi Dewan blog; or an internal contradiction inside ms-register.md / owner-vocabulary-rules.md. Items without evidence are recorded under confirmedStrong, not as issues. Findings already made in ms-register-audit-checklist.json (laluan pilihan, disokong vs diperakukan, Sep vs Sept, Pengurus yang Sedang Bekerja, ialah/adalah, article calques, month abbreviations, regex checks) are not repeated; where a new finding builds on one of them the cross-reference is stated. An earlier draft found at this path was re-verified line by line and merged: its claims that survived verification are included with the URLs re-fetched here, and the items dropped or overridden are listed under droppedFromEarlierDraft. Governance facts (RM10,000.00; scholarship selective and confirmed individually in writing, no amounts; CMI Certificate of Recognition, not an MQA-accredited degree; six months, six training days, three sessions, applied project; HRD Corp employer-led) are untouched by every correction below. owner-vocabulary-rules.md (2026-09-04) overrides this file and the sibling audit where they differ; the differences are named in missingRules 'Owner pattern'.

issues.rule: Use 'Sebab itu', 'Jadi', 'Justeru', 'Oleh itu' as connectives; the first two for warm pages, the last two for formal pages.
issues.problem: 'Justeru' is offered as a formal twin of 'Oleh itu' (therefore). Kamus Dewan gives it two senses only: 'kebetulan, tepat, kena benar' and 'malahan, bahkan' (in fact, moreover); there is no consequence sense. A Munsyi Dewan calls the sentence-initial 'therefore' use ungrammatical, and DBP's advisory line, as reproduced by teachers, tolerates 'Justeru,' only in the dictionary sense and rejects 'justeru itu'. An agent following Do 13 will write 'Justeru, yuran disahkan secara bertulis' meaning 'therefore', which a DBP-literate KL reader parses as 'in fact' — on fee, HRD Corp or CMI sentences that is a change of meaning, not of tone.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=justeru — Kamus Dewan Edisi Keempat: '1. kebetulan, tepat, kena benar … 2. malahan, bahkan'; http://abrahimblog.blogspot.com/2012/07/justeru-penanda-wacana-atau-kata-hubung.html — Munsyi Dewan (28 Julai 2012): sentence-initial discourse-marker use is 'tidak gramatis'; http://koleksicikguharlina.blogspot.com/2019/05/justeru-atau-justeru-itu.html — DBP reply reproduced: use 'justeru' with a comma, never 'justeru itu'
issues.correction: Formal consequence connectives are 'Oleh itu,' and 'Oleh sebab itu,' (Kamus Dewan: 'oleh sebab itu = lantaran itu'). Allow 'Justeru,' only where the meaning is 'malahan/bahkan', always followed by a comma; ban 'justeru itu'. Add `\bjusteru itu\b` to the checklist-6 ban list and flag any 'Justeru' that opens a fee, HRD Corp or CMI sentence for a meaning check.

issues.rule: 'Sebab itu' … for warm pages.
issues.problem: Bare 'Sebab itu,' is the spoken shortening the guide copied from the Siti Khadijah blog (2.5). Kamus Dewan lists the conjunction as 'oleh sebab itu' ('lantaran itu'); the 'sebab' entry shows only the 'oleh sebab …' construction. On a hero page addressed to directors and owners, 'Sebab itu,' sits one register below the 'warm-formal' target the same table sets; no fetched source outside the telekung blog uses it in body copy.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=oleh%20sebab%20itu — Kamus Dewan: 'oleh sebab itu: lantaran itu'; https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=sebab — entry shows 'oleh ~ kerana', no bare 'sebab itu'; ms-register.md 2.5 (the only source of 'Sebab itu' is sitikhadijah.com blog copy)
issues.correction: Hero and programme pages: 'Oleh sebab itu,' or 'Itulah sebabnya' (warm but standard). Keep bare 'Sebab itu,' for campaign landing pages and nurture e-mails only, at most once per page. 'Jadi,' stays allowed in e-mail and campaign copy (Kamus Dewan 'jadi' sense 5 '= jadinya kerananya, kerana itu'), not in hero blocks.

issues.section: 4 row 48 (also 2.3 DBP checks; checklist 6 ban on 'kepemimpinan'; sibling audit missingRule 'servant leadership')
issues.rule: leadership → kepimpinan; Not 'kepemimpinan'; 2.3: 'kepemimpinan is not the headword'.
issues.problem: The factual claim is false. Kamus Dewan Edisi Keempat has a full entry for 'kepemimpinan' ('keupayaan (kebolehan, pencapaian, dsb) sbg pemimpin'), Kamus Pelajar has it too, and DBP's own Istilah renders 'servant leadership' as 'kepemimpinan kebaktian' (Pentadbiran). Preferring 'kepimpinan' is right for Malaysian usage (news, universities, HRD Corp), but it is a consistency choice, not a DBP ruling; the sibling audit repeats the error by calling 'kepemimpinan' Indonesian. An agent told 'DBP rejects it' will 'correct' quotations, book titles or partner text that legitimately use it.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=kepemimpinan — Kamus Dewan Edisi Keempat: 'keupayaan (kebolehan, pencapaian, dsb) sbg pemimpin'; Kamus Pelajar Edisi Kedua: 'hal-hal yg berkaitan dgn pemimpin'; https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1.aspx?keyword=servant+leadership&d=371752 — Istilah Bahasa Melayu: servant leadership = 'kepemimpinan kebaktian' (Pentadbiran); ms-register.md 3.17 shows 'kepimpinan: keupayaan memimpin' (both are headwords)
issues.correction: Reword row 48 and 2.3: 'kepimpinan — site-wide form, chosen for consistency with Malaysian news, university and HRD Corp usage; kepemimpinan is also a Kamus Dewan headword (and DBP Istilah's form) but is not used in site-authored copy.' Keep the checklist-6 ban as a consistency check and exempt verbatim quotations and third-party titles.

issues.rule: Allowable Cost Matrix — keep English; HRD Corp BM label 'Kos Matriks yang dibenarkan' may follow in brackets.
issues.problem: The guide records only the calque. The same HRD Corp Garis Panduan page also carries the grammatical Malay form 'Matriks Kos Yang Dibenarkan' (head noun first). If a BM gloss is added, row 28 steers the agent to the ungrammatical variant.
issues.evidence: https://hrdcorp.gov.my/ms/guidelines-bm — page shows both 'Kos Matriks yang dibenarkan' and 'Matriks Kos Yang Dibenarkan'; footer 'PEMBANGUNAN SUMBER MANUSIA BERHAD'
issues.correction: Row 28: 'Allowable Cost Matrix (Matriks Kos yang Dibenarkan)' on first mention per page, English identifier alone thereafter. Note in 2.3 that HRD Corp uses both labels and that the site follows the head-noun-first form.

issues.rule: Site's 'terakreditasi MQA' is acceptable; pick one form.
issues.problem: 'terakreditasi' is not a DBP form. Kamus Dewan derives only 'mengakreditasi' ('memberikan akreditasi kpd sesebuah institusi dsb'), whose passive is 'diakreditasi'; PRPM returns no entry for 'terakreditasi' (it is the Indonesian BAN-PT usage 'terakreditasi A'). MQA's own BM FAQ uses 'akreditasi', 'diakredit' and 'swaakreditasi'. Declaring 'terakreditasi' acceptable invites the Indonesian form onto the sentence the governance file guards most (not an MQA-accredited degree).
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=akreditasi — Kamus Dewan: 'mengakreditasi memberikan akreditasi kpd sesebuah institusi dsb'; https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=terakreditasi — 'Tiada maklumat tesaurus untuk kata terakreditasi', no Kamus Dewan entry; https://www.mqa.gov.my/new/bm/faq_permohonanakr.cfm — 'untuk mendapatkan akreditasi', 'berstatus swaakreditasi'
issues.correction: Row 32: 'bukan ijazah akademik yang diakreditasi oleh MQA' only; add `\bterakreditasi\b` to the checklist-6 ban list; 'berakreditasi penuh' / 'akreditasi sementara' only when quoting a university badge verbatim.

issues.section: 5 Do 7 (also Section 3 PDF row, intake rows in 6.15, sibling audit missingRule 'Availability and cohort labels')
issues.rule: Write dates as '22–23 Ogos 2026', '9 pagi hingga 6 petang', 'Sabtu dan Ahad'.
issues.problem: '9 pagi' is newspaper shorthand. DBP's advisory service gives the written standard as 'pukul 9.00 pagi' and 'dari pukul 9.00 pagi hingga 2.00 petang'. Intake rows, the fees page, the PDF guide and e-mails are exactly the formal contexts where the DBP form belongs; the sibling audit's cohort-label example copies the shorthand.
issues.evidence: https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=9.00%20pagi&d=10 — DBP Khidmat Nasihat: 'Penggunaan yang betul ialah pukul 9.00 pagi'; 'dari pukul 9.00 pagi hingga 2.00 petang'
issues.correction: Intake rows, fees page, PDF and e-mails: '9.00 pagi hingga 6.00 petang'. '9 pagi' allowed only inside a headline or campaign hook. Update the sibling audit's example to 'Sabtu dan Ahad, 9.00 pagi hingga 6.00 petang' and the BM renderer map ('9am' → '9.00 pagi', '6pm' → '6.00 petang').

issues.rule: sign-off 'Salam hormat, Pasukan Program Future Ready Executive MBA'.
issues.problem: 'Salam hormat' is a commercial habit, not the standard closing. DBP's advisory service says the closing is 'Sekian' with no further salam after it; the Ministry of National Unity's 2022 circular on letters, memos and e-mail closes 'Sekian, terima kasih.' before the signature block; Jobstreet's guides give 'Sekian, terima kasih.' and 'Yang benar,' as the closings. A programme team writing to directors should not close less formally than a jobs portal recommends.
issues.evidence: https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=salam%20hormat&d=10 — DBP Khidmat Nasihat: 'Penutup surat ungkapan sekian. Tiada lagi ucapan salam selepas itu'; https://www.perpaduan.gov.my/images/document/muat-turun/SURAT_EDARAN-GARIS_PANDUAN_PENULISAN_SURAT_RASMI_MEMO_PERHUBUNGAN.pdf (KPN, 14 Februari 2022) — closes 'Sekian, terima kasih.' then 'Saya yang menjalankan amanah,'; https://my.jobstreet.com/career-advice/article/panduan-contoh-ayat-email-hantar-dokumen — closings 'Sekian, terima kasih.' and 'Yang benar,'
issues.correction: Acknowledgement e-mail: 'Sekian, terima kasih.' on its own line, then 'Pasukan Program Future Ready Executive MBA'. Nurture e-mails (warm-formal): 'Terima kasih,' then the team name. Drop 'Salam hormat'; 'Yang benar,' only on signed letters. Update Section 3, Do 17 and checklist 13.

issues.rule: Salutation 'Salam sejahtera, {Nama},' (fallback 'Tuan/Puan').
issues.problem: Two defects. (a) A bare given name after the greeting is informal for owners and directors; Malaysian practice is 'Tuan/Puan' or an honorific plus name, and the guide gives no honorific rule at all (no field for Datuk/Dato'/Dr., no Encik/Puan/Cik). (b) The comma after 'Salam sejahtera' is not the Malaysian pattern: Jobstreet writes 'Salam Sejahtera Tuan / Puan' and the government form is the vocative alone ('Tuan/Puan,'). The fallback is right; the named form is under-specified.
issues.evidence: https://my.jobstreet.com/career-advice/article/panduan-contoh-ayat-email-hantar-dokumen — greeting 'Salam Sejahtera Tuan / Puan'; https://www.perpaduan.gov.my/images/document/muat-turun/SURAT_EDARAN-GARIS_PANDUAN_PENULISAN_SURAT_RASMI_MEMO_PERHUBUNGAN.pdf — kata sapaan 'Tuan,' / 'YBhg. Tan Sri/ Datuk/ Dato'/ Dr./ Tuan/ Puan,', address line '(u.p.: Encik Megat Harris Shah bin Zahari)'; https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=Encik — Kamus Dewan: 'panggilan kpd orang lelaki yg sederhana kedudukannya atau yg tidak dikenali'
issues.correction: Default 'Salam sejahtera Tuan/Puan,' (no comma after sejahtera). When the form captures a title, 'Salam sejahtera {gelaran} {Nama},' — 'Salam sejahtera Puan Aina Rahman,', 'Salam sejahtera Dr. Kumar,', 'Salam sejahtera YBhg. Datuk Ahmad,'. Never a bare first name. Add the honorifics rule (missingRules) and a title field to the enquiry form or fall back to Tuan/Puan.

issues.section: 5 Do 8 (also Section 3 campaign row model sentence)
issues.rule: Use numerals for programme facts in running text and headlines (6 bulan, 3 sesi, 12 modul), as news and universities do; words only for one-off small counts.
issues.problem: Stated as if standard, but DBP's advisory service says one to nine are spelled out in prose and numerals start at 10. Numerals for the fixed programme facts are a defensible house style (content.ts, EN/ZH parity, headline practice), but the guide neither says it is a deviation nor states the exception it already relies on: the Section 3 campaign model opens 'Enam bulan. Tiga hujung minggu.' with spelled-out numbers, which Do 8 as written forbids. An agent applying Do 8 will 'fix' the model to '6 bulan. 3 hujung minggu.'
issues.evidence: https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=angka&d=10 — DBP Khidmat Nasihat: 'nombor dari satu hingga sembilan hendaklah dieja penuh'; 'nombor 10 dan keatas hendaklah ditulis dengan angka'; ms-register.md Section 3 campaign row: 'Enam bulan. Tiga hujung minggu. Satu projek perniagaan anda sendiri.'
issues.correction: Rewrite Do 8: 'House style (deviates from DBP for consistency with content.ts, the EN and ZH pages and headline practice): numerals for the fixed programme facts — 6 bulan, 6 hari latihan, 3 sesi, 12 modul — in headlines, tables, intake rows and fact sentences. Exceptions: a number that opens a sentence or fragment is spelled out (Enam bulan.) or the sentence is restructured (Tempoh 6 bulan, 3 sesi hujung minggu); a count of one is a word (satu projek); insights articles follow DBP (one to nine in words).' Add a checklist test: no body sentence begins with a numeral.

issues.rule: Write money as RM10,000.00 (no space, comma thousands, two decimals…); Don't write 'RM 10,000', 'RM10 000' or '10,000 ringgit'.
issues.problem: The no-space rule is DBP-correct. The comma rule is not: DBP's advisory service prescribes a space, not a comma, as the thousands separator ('10 000'), so Don't 30 bans DBP's own form and the guide's only evidence for the comma is newspaper practice. The site must keep 'RM10,000.00' because the governance file fixes that string and Malaysian banks and newspapers use the comma; the defect is that the guide claims a standard it does not have and gives the agent no reason to resist a future 'correction' to DBP spacing.
issues.evidence: https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=RM&d=10 — DBP Khidmat Nasihat: 'Cara menulis RM berserta nombor perlu dirapatkan, contohnya RM10.00 atau RM10'; https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=angka&d=10 — 'tiada koma tetapi dijarakkan seperti 10 000'; SEO-CONTENT-GOVERNANCE.md 'Publish RM10,000.00 as the standard fee' (as cited in ms-register-audit-checklist.json 7.4)
issues.correction: No change to any amount (RM10,000.00 stays verbatim). Reword Do 6 / Don't 30: 'RM attached to the figure (DBP). Comma thousands and two decimals follow the governance label and Malaysian banking practice, not DBP, which prefers a space; the site never mixes the two, and never the Indonesian 10.000,00.'

issues.section: 3 Insights articles row (model sentence) versus 5 Don't 32 and checklist 5
issues.rule: Model sentence: 'Pengurus kanan jarang kekurangan data; yang sering kurang ialah kaedah untuk menukar data kepada satu keputusan yang boleh dipertanggungjawabkan.'
issues.problem: The guide's own model contains 'sering', which Don't 32 bans and checklist 5 greps for, plus 'jarang' (same frequency-qualifier class) and the article calque 'satu keputusan' the sibling audit flags. An agent that copies Section 3 fails Section 7 on the same text. Underlying cause: Don't 32 is written as a register rule when its source is governance, which forbids qualifiers on facts and outcomes, not frequency adverbs in editorial prose.
issues.evidence: ms-register.md Don't 32 ('sering' listed) and checklist 5 regex `biasanya|kebiasaannya|selalunya|sering|kebanyakan…`; ms-register-audit-checklist.json missingRule 'Article calques' and 7.5
issues.correction: Model sentence: 'Pengurus kanan tidak kekurangan data. Yang kurang ialah kaedah untuk menukar data kepada keputusan yang boleh dipertanggungjawabkan.' Scope Don't 32 and checklist 5: absolute ban in any sentence carrying a site fact, a number, a reader outcome or a claim about readers ('Kebanyakan pembaca …'); in insights body prose 'sering/jarang' may appear only in a general observation with no number or outcome attached, and never in the model.

issues.section: 3 Acknowledgement and nurture e-mails row (model sentence)
issues.rule: '… satu perbualan ringkas biasanya cukup — tanpa bayaran dan tanpa komitmen pendaftaran.' (remove 'biasanya' if governance treats it as a qualifier …)
issues.problem: The guide ships a model with 'biasanya' and defers the decision, although its own Don't 32 and checklist 5 ban 'biasanya' outright and the sibling audit confirms governance treats it as a qualifier. A model sentence must be the passing form. 'satu perbualan ringkas' also carries the article calque ('satu' = 'a').
issues.evidence: ms-register.md Don't 32 and checklist 5 (both list 'biasanya'); ms-register-audit-checklist.json 7.5 and missingRule 'Article calques'
issues.correction: Model: 'Beberapa hari lalu anda meminta panduan program. Jika ada bahagian yang kurang jelas, perbualan ringkas dapat menjelaskannya — tanpa bayaran dan tanpa komitmen pendaftaran.' Delete the bracketed hedge.

issues.section: 5 Do 18 (versus Do 16, row 68 and every CTA in Section 3)
issues.rule: Keep sentence-case headlines; Title Case only for named documents and CTAs.
issues.problem: Do 18 makes CTAs Title Case, but every CTA the guide prescribes is sentence case ('Dapatkan panduan program 2026', 'Tempah sesi perbincangan program', 'Hantar pertanyaan untuk syarikat anda'), while row 68 gives Title Case 'Ketahui Lebih Lanjut'. Two agents will ship two button styles. If Title Case is kept anywhere, the guide also omits DBP's rule that function words stay lowercase.
issues.evidence: ms-register.md Do 16 and Section 3 CTA column (sentence case) versus row 68 and Do 18; https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=huruf%20besar%20tajuk&d=10 — DBP Khidmat Nasihat: 'kata sendi sahaja yang harus dieja dalam huruf kecil', example 'Pujangga yang Malang'
issues.correction: Sentence case for all CTAs and headings (matches the site and news practice). Title Case only for named documents ('Panduan Program 2026') and official titles, with 'yang, dan, untuk, di, ke, kepada, daripada, dengan, atau, bagi, adalah' lowercase. Change row 68 to 'Ketahui lebih lanjut'.

issues.rule: Gloss an English official term once per page in brackets, MQA-style: 'Daftar Kelayakan Malaysia (Malaysian Qualifications Register, MQR)'.
issues.problem: The example runs the opposite way from the rule: MQA puts the Malay name first and the English in brackets, whereas Do 2 and rows 3/38 keep the English identifier first with a Malay gloss in brackets. The owner's vocabulary rule adds a third case (Malay concept first, English in brackets: 'kepimpinan berkhidmat (servant leadership)'). Do 3 gives no way to decide which direction applies, so one page can carry 'CMI Certificate of Recognition (sijil pengiktirafan CMI)' and 'sijil pengiktirafan CMI (CMI Certificate of Recognition)'.
issues.evidence: ms-register.md Do 2, Do 3, rows 3 and 38; owner-vocabulary-rules.md: 'Local term first, English in round brackets on first use on a page'; MQA 3.9 pattern quoted in ms-register.md 2.3
issues.correction: Split Do 3 into three directions: (a) official identifiers (certificate names, HRD Corp products, CMI titles, system names) — English first, verbatim, Malay gloss in brackets once per page, then English alone; (b) Malaysian bodies — Malay name first, English name and acronym in brackets once (MQA style); (c) owner messaging vocabulary and any concept the site coins — Malay term first, English in brackets once, then Malay alone (owner rule). Never both directions for one term on one page. See missingRules 'Programme name…' and 'Owner pattern…'.

issues.rule: Use 'pemohon' for the person before enrolment.
issues.problem: 'pemohon' means someone who has applied ('orang yg memohon sesuatu'). Before enrolment most readers have only requested a guide or sent an enquiry, and the guide's own Don't 33 and the governance file insist an enquiry is not an application. Calling a guide-requester 'pemohon' in nurture e-mails or the FAQ implies an application exists. 'pemohon' is right only for the scholarship, a place or the HRD Corp grant (where HRD Corp itself uses 'pemohon').
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=pemohon — Kamus Dewan: 'orang yg memohon sesuatu'; Kamus Pelajar: 'orang yg memohon; peminta'; ms-register.md Don't 33 ('an enquiry is not an application')
issues.correction: Do 15: 'peserta' inside the programme; 'pemohon' only for someone who has applied for a place, the scholarship or an HRD Corp grant; enquirers and guide readers are 'anda' (third person: 'pembaca'); 'majikan' for the funding party. Add to checklist 18: 'pemohon' may not appear in nurture e-mails or on the enquiry form.

issues.rule: 'para pengurus', 'para peserta' only in speeches or invitation headlines; on web pages use plain 'pengurus', 'peserta'.
issues.problem: 'para' is the standard plural marker and Kamus Dewan's own example is 'para peserta'. It is normal in formal web copy where plurality or a collective address matters ('para majikan berdaftar HRD Corp'). A blanket ban is a house choice presented as a norm, and it removes the one device that disambiguates singular from plural in sentences without a numeral.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=para — Kamus Dewan Edisi Keempat: 'kata (yg mendahului kata-kata lain) yg menyatakan ramai: ~ mahasiswa dan pelajar; ~ peserta'
issues.correction: Allow 'para' + human noun where the sentence addresses or counts a group ('para peserta kohort Oktober', 'para majikan berdaftar HRD Corp'); bare noun in generic statements ('peserta menyelesaikan 6 hari latihan'); never 'para' with an 'anda' sentence and never with a reduplicated plural (sibling audit rule).

issues.rule: Row 6: intake → pengambilan, 'Sesi pengambilan for an intake window'; row 5: kohort, 'not sesi'; row 8: session (live) → sesi.
issues.problem: On this site 'sesi' already means one of the three weekend sessions ('3 sesi hujung minggu'). Recommending 'sesi pengambilan' (a real corpus phrase, 4.3 and 4.6) puts 'sesi' into the same paragraph in two senses and re-creates the ambiguity that 6.9 corrects ('Pilih sesi …' → 'Pilih kohort …').
issues.evidence: ms-register.md rows 5, 6, 8 and 6.9; corpus 'Sesi pengambilan pelajar dilakukan dua kali (2X) setahun' (4.3) is genuine but not needed here
issues.correction: Reserve 'sesi' for the training sessions; write the intake as 'pengambilan Oktober 2026' / 'tarikh pengambilan', and the dated group as 'kohort'. Delete 'Sesi pengambilan' from row 6.

issues.section: 5 Don't 28 ('berbaloi' listed as a tabloid hook) and 6 further items (H decisionAside)
issues.rule: Don't use tabloid hooks: … 'berbaloi' …; 6: 'berbaloi' is deals vocabulary and shifts the EN meaning.
issues.problem: Two different claims are fused. The register claim is wrong: Kamus Dewan lists 'berbaloi' as 'berpadanan, seimbang' with no colloquial or slang label, and the site already uses it neutrally elsewhere ('bahagian mana yang paling berbaloi anda kembangkan', 'kekangan … yang berbaloi ditangani'), which Don't 28 would now fail. The meaning claim for the decisionAside sentence is right: the EN says the guide helps the reader decide whether the programme deserves a conversation, so 'sama ada program ini berbaloi untuk anda' (worth it for you) is a value-for-money reframing and the guide's fix 'wajar dibincangkan' is the faithful one.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=berbaloi — Kamus Dewan: 'berpadanan, seimbang', no register label; src/components/site/FutureCommerceHome.tsx line 53 (EN decisionAside 'whether the programme deserves one') and line 96 (BM 'berbaloi untuk anda'); src/app/(ms)/ms/lp/google/page.tsx and mba-for-sme-owners/page.tsx (neutral 'berbaloi' uses)
issues.correction: Move 'berbaloi' out of the tabloid list into a governance rule: banned where it frames the programme, the fee, a discount or a return ('program ini berbaloi', 'yuran berbaloi', 'pelaburan berbaloi'); allowed for effort or priority judgements with no money in view ('bahagian yang paling berbaloi anda kembangkan'). Keep the decisionAside fix ('wajar dibincangkan lebih lanjut') on EN-equivalence grounds.

issues.section: 4 row 39 and 5 Do 19 (builds on sibling audit 6.3, not a repeat)
issues.rule: 'diperakukan' is the official-endorsement verb.
issues.problem: The sibling audit showed Kamus Dewan defines 'memperakukan' through 'menyokong' (support, recommend). The verb the guide may have been reaching for is 'memperakui', which Kamus Dewan glosses 'mengesahkan' ('diperakui oleh undang-undang'). That is an attestation verb: 'diperakui oleh CMI' would tell a Malaysian reader the certificate is certified/validated by CMI, one step closer to the accreditation reading the governance file forbids. So neither 'diperakukan' nor 'diperakui' improves on 'disokong'.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=memperakui — Kamus Dewan: 'mengesahkan: lantikan tersebut adalah sah dan diperakui oleh undang-undang'; ms-register-audit-checklist.json 6.3 (memperakukan = 'memberikan sokongan … menyokong'; endorse = 'menyokong')
issues.correction: Row 39 / Do 19: 'dianugerahkan dan disokong oleh CMI' site-wide (one verb); ban both 'diperakukan oleh CMI' and 'diperakui oleh CMI' in the checklist-6 list; 'diiktiraf' only with 'berdasarkan CMI Professional Standards'; 'diakreditasi' MQA only.

issues.rule: Don't use 'dalam bentuk bertulis' (row 20: 'Not dalam bentuk bertulis'); 6.5 calls it a calque.
issues.problem: DBP has no ruling against 'dalam bentuk bertulis'; its advisory archive uses 'secara bertulis' and 'kebenaran bertulis' in its own answers and does not mark the longer phrase as wrong, and the phrase is common in Malaysian government acts and FAQs (search across gov.my). 'secara bertulis' is the better default for brevity and matches MQA/HRD Corp, but labelling the longer form a calque overstates it, and an agent will 'correct' quoted terms-and-conditions text that legitimately uses it.
issues.evidence: https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=dalam%20bentuk%20bertulis&d=10 — DBP's own answers use 'secara bertulis' and 'kebenaran bertulis'; no ruling on 'dalam bentuk bertulis'; WebSearch '"dalam bentuk bertulis" site:gov.my' returns acts and guideline PDFs using the phrase (not individually fetched)
issues.correction: Row 20 / Don't 24: prefer 'secara bertulis' / 'kelulusan bertulis' in site copy; treat 'dalam bentuk bertulis' as an acceptable formal variant, not an error, and exempt quoted legal text. Keep the 6.5 rewrite for its other reasons ('anugerah', 'tidak automatik').

issues.rule: employer-led / employer-funded → diterajui majikan / pembiayaan majikan.
issues.problem: 'menerajui' means to head or lead an organisation or movement, so 'diterajui majikan' says the employer heads the programme. The HRD Corp fact is procedural: the employer submits the grant application and the claim. 'pembiayaan majikan' is fine; 'diterajui' is not.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=menerajui — Kamus Dewan: 'memegang teraju pimpinan, memimpin, mengetuai, mengendalikan', example '~ sebuah organisasi yg besar'; HRD Corp SBL page as quoted in ms-register.md 2.3: 'haruslah dihantar oleh majikan sebelum tarikh latihan bermula'
issues.correction: Row 22: employer-led → 'dipohon oleh majikan' / 'melalui majikan' (permohonan geran dan tuntutan dibuat oleh majikan); employer-funded → 'pembiayaan majikan' / 'dibiayai majikan'. Keep the site's 'Laluan pembiayaan majikan'. Drop 'diterajui'.

issues.rule: request a corporate proposal → minta cadangan korporat.
issues.problem: 'cadangan' covers suggestion, motion and proposal alike (Kamus Inggeris-Melayu Dewan for 'proposal': 'cadangan, usul, saranan, anjuran'), and 'korporat' is an adjective ('berkaitan dgn syarikat atau perbadanan'), so 'cadangan korporat' reads as 'a corporate suggestion' rather than a priced document for the company. Malaysian business usage names the document 'kertas cadangan'.
issues.evidence: https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=proposal — 'cadangan, usul, saranan, anjuran'; https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=korporat — Kamus Dewan: 'berkaitan dgn syarikat atau perbadanan'

missingRules.topic: Numbers in prose: words, numerals, sentence starts, ranges, decimals, percent, ordinals
missingRules.rule: DBP: one to nine in words, 10 and above in numerals, in running prose; a body sentence or fragment never opens with a numeral (spell it — 'Enam bulan …' — or restructure: 'Tempoh 6 bulan, 3 sesi hujung minggu'); the house exception (Do 8 rewrite) keeps numerals for the fixed programme facts in headlines, tables, intake rows and fact sentences. Ranges: unspaced en dash in headings, tables and short lines ('6–12 bulan', '22–23 Ogos 2026'), 'hingga' in running prose ('dari 22 hingga 23 Ogos 2026'), never a spaced hyphen or English 'to'. Decimals take a point ('1.23 peratus'), never a comma; 'peratus' spelled in prose, '%' only in tables, no space before '%'. Ordinals: words below 10 in prose ('sesi kedua', 'hari ketiga'), 'ke-' with a hyphen from 10 ('kohort ke-17'), 'ke-' forms in tables ('Sesi ke-3'); a named cohort is a cardinal label ('Kohort 17'), the counting sense takes 'ke-' ('kohort ke-17 sejak 2013'); never 'ke 17', 'ke17', '17hb'. Fail: `(^|\. )\d` at sentence start in body copy; `\d+,\d+ peratus`; `\bke ?\d`; `\d ?%` outside a table cell; `\d - \d`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Enam bulan, tiga sesi hujung minggu, 12 modul.'; 'Kohort 17 bermula pada 22 Ogos 2026.'; 'Ini kohort ke-17 sejak program diperkenalkan.'; table cell '1%' rendered in prose as '1 peratus'. Fail: '6 bulan …' opening a body sentence; 'kohort ke 17'; 'naik 2,5 peratus'; '6 - 12 bulan'. (Evidence: DBP Khidmat Nasihat k=angka, k=peratus; PRPM 'sempang')

missingRules.rule: RM attached to the figure (DBP). The standard fee is always the governance string 'RM10,000.00' verbatim; every other RM figure copies its style (comma thousands; two decimals only when the source label carries them; 'RM17 juta' style for rounded large sums in articles); never the Indonesian '10.000,00'. RM is the only currency marker in BM copy ('MYR' only inside bank-transfer or payment-gateway fields). Never 'RM10k', 'RM10 ribu', '10,000 ringgit', 'RM10K'. Repeat RM at both ends of a range ('RM8,000–RM10,000' in tables, 'RM8,000 hingga RM10,000' in prose). Per-unit with 'seorang' / 'bagi setiap peserta' / 'sebulan' after the amount, never 'per'. Cents are 'sen' ('50 sen', not 'RM0.50' in prose); amounts in words only on invoices or receipts, in the DBP form 'Ringgit Malaysia: sepuluh ribu sahaja'. No plural or possessive on RM. Never derive new amounts (monthly instalment figures, fee after scholarship) from the fee — governance forbids new numbers. Fail: `RM\s?\d+\s?(k|K|ribu)\b`; `\bMYR\b` outside form fields; `RM0\.\d\d`; `\d ringgit\b`; `\bper (peserta|orang|bulan)\b`; `\d\.\d{3},\d\d`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Yuran standard ialah RM10,000.00 seorang, disahkan secara bertulis oleh pasukan program.'; 'pelaburan terkumpul melebihi RM17 juta' (article). Fail: 'RM10k'; 'MYR 10,000'; 'RM 10,000.00'; 'RM10,000 per peserta'; 'RM833 sebulan' (derived number). (Evidence: DBP Khidmat Nasihat k=RM; SEO-CONTENT-GOVERNANCE.md fee string)

missingRules.rule: Clock times in the DBP form '9.00 pagi hingga 6.00 petang' ('pukul' optional in tables; never am/pm or 24-hour in BM copy); 'tengah hari' for 12.00–1.59 (12.00 is tengah hari, not petang), 'petang' 2.00–6.59, 'malam' from 7.00. Days 'Sabtu dan Ahad' / 'Jumaat dan Sabtu' (never 'Minggu' for Sunday, never 'Sat–Sun'); 'hujung minggu' for weekend; day name before the date with a comma ('Sabtu, 22 Ogos 2026'). Dates day-month-year with full month names in prose ('22 Ogos 2026'), no 'hb' ('22hb' is dated civil-service style), en dash for date ranges in tables ('22–23 Ogos'), 'hingga' in prose; DBP abbreviations (Jan., Feb., Mac, Apr., Mei, Jun, Jul., Ogos, Sept., Okt., Nov., Dis.) only in tables — never 'Sep' (sibling audit 6.15, PRPM 'Sept'). The year appears once per sentence; no time zone. Fail: `\d\s?(am|pm)\b`; `\b(Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)\b`; `\bMinggu\b` as a day name; `\d{1,2}hb\b`; `\b\d{1,2} (pagi|petang|malam)\b` outside headlines; `\bSep\b`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Sabtu dan Ahad, 9.00 pagi hingga 6.00 petang.'; 'Sesi pertama: 22–23 Ogos 2026.' (table); 'Sesi pertama berlangsung pada 22 hingga 23 Ogos 2026.' (prose). Fail: 'Sat–Sun 9am–6pm'; 'Sabtu dan Minggu'; '22hb Ogos'; '9 pagi hingga 6 petang' in an intake row. (Evidence: DBP Khidmat Nasihat k=9.00 pagi)

missingRules.rule: Follow Surat Pekeliling Am Bil. 4 Tahun 2014 (Jabatan Perdana Menteri, 30 Jun 2014), which applies to 'Kementerian/Jabatan/Agensi Kerajaan dan swasta'. Federal awards: Tun → 'YABhg.'; Tan Sri, Puan Sri, Datuk, Datin → 'YBhg.'; royal descent (Tunku, Tengku, Raja) → 'YM'; Syed/Sheikh → 'Tuan', Sharifah/Siti → 'Puan/Cik'; Haji → 'Tuan', Hajah → 'Puan'. Academics: 'YBrs. Dr. diikuti dengan nama', 'YBrs. Prof. Madya Dr.', 'YBhg. Datuk Prof. Madya Dr.', 'YBhg. Tan Sri Prof. Dr.' — so the order when titles combine is [YBhg./YBrs.] [gelaran kebesaran] [Prof./Prof. Madya] [Dr.] [Haji/Hajah] Nama. Abbreviations that mix capitals and lowercase take a full stop ('YBhg.', 'YBrs.', 'Dr.', 'Prof.', 'Ir.', 'Ts.'); 'Dato'' with the apostrophe (state award), 'Datuk' without (federal). Untitled adults: 'Encik' / 'Puan' / 'Cik' + name in address lines and bios ('u.p.: Encik Megat Harris Shah bin Zahari' in the KPN circular), 'Tuan/Puan' as the salutation. Web body copy drops 'YBhg./YBrs.' and keeps the title ('Datuk Dr. Ahmad Kamal'); faculty bios 'Dr. Nama', never 'Doktor Nama'; English post-nominals (fCMgr, CMgr) after the name with no comma. Malay names: honorific + given name ('Encik Ahmad', not 'Encik bin Ali'); Chinese names: honorific + surname ('Puan Tan'); Indian names: honorific + given name ('Encik Kumar'). Never 'Bapak' / 'Ibu' (Indonesian), never 'Mr' / 'Mrs' inside BM copy. Fail: `\b(Bapak|Ibu) [A-Z]`; `\bDoktor [A-Z]`; `\bY\.Bhg\b|\bYBhg\b(?!\.)`; `\bDato\b(?!')`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Salam sejahtera Tuan/Puan,'; 'Salam sejahtera YBhg. Datuk Ahmad,' (e-mail with title field); 'Fasilitator: Datuk Dr. Ahmad Kamal, Pengerusi, Syarikat X' (web bio); 'Puan Nur Aisyah, Pengurus Besar' (testimonial byline). Fail: 'Y.Bhg Dato Ahmad'; 'Doktor Ahmad Kamal'; 'Bapak Ahmad'. (Evidence: https://www.istiadat.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/SP-Am-Bil-4-Tahun-2014-Panggilan-Hormat-dan-Kaedah-Pengggunaannya.pdf, Lampiran B–F; KPN circular PDF; https://ecentral.my/panggilan-hormat/)

missingRules.topic: E-mail frame: opening, closing, signature, subject
missingRules.rule: Opening: 'Salam sejahtera Tuan/Puan,' or 'Salam sejahtera {gelaran} {Nama},'; no 'Dengan hormatnya' (letter register) and no religious greeting by default (mixed audience). Closing: acknowledgement e-mail 'Sekian, terima kasih.' on its own line; nurture e-mail 'Terima kasih,'; then 'Pasukan Program Future Ready Executive MBA' with the WhatsApp and e-mel lines; no 'Salam hormat', no 'Yang benar' (signed letters only), no slogan lines. Subject line: sentence case, no full stop, at most 10 words, no exclamation, the programme name verbatim. Contact strings: '+60 12-345 6789' grouping, 'melalui WhatsApp' / 'melalui e-mel' with 'melalui', 'laman web' not 'website'. Fail: `Salam hormat`, `Dengan hormatnya`, `Yang benar` in e-mail templates; `!$` in a subject; `\bwebsite\b`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Sekian, terima kasih.' / 'Pasukan Program Future Ready Executive MBA' / 'Hubungi kami melalui WhatsApp di +60 12-345 6789 atau e-mel.' Subject: 'Panduan program 2026 yang anda minta'. Fail: 'Salam hormat, Pasukan Program …'; subject 'Panduan Program 2026 Anda Sudah Tiba!'. (Evidence: DBP Khidmat Nasihat k=salam hormat; KPN circular)

missingRules.rule: H1/H2 never end with a full stop; a colon may split promise and object ('Panduan program 2026: yuran, kohort dan laluan HRD Corp'); a spaced em dash for one sub-clause, consistent with the guide's own H1 fix ('Yuran standard RM10,000.00 — biasiswa terhad, tertakluk kepada penilaian kelayakan'); no semicolon (sibling 7.15), no ampersand, no exclamation, no ellipsis, no quotation-mark hooks; question marks only on FAQ H2/H3 and campaign H2s; en dash for ranges inside headlines ('22–23 Ogos'); no quotation marks or italics around identifiers or English terms in headings (Do 2); a numeral may open a headline ('6 bulan, 3 sesi, 1 projek') although a body sentence may not — but do not open an H1 with a numeral if the same words recur as a body sentence. Sentence case for headings and CTAs; Title Case only for named documents, with DBP's function-word rule ('yang, dan, untuk, di, ke, kepada, daripada, dengan, atau, bagi, adalah' lowercase). Fail: `[.!;&…]$` on a heading string; `^["']|["']$` in headings; `\b(Yang|Dan|Untuk|Di|Ke|Adalah)\b` mid-title; ` - ` (spaced hyphen) in a heading.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Executive MBA 6 bulan untuk pengurus yang bekerja sepenuh masa'; 'Bolehkah majikan saya menuntut yuran daripada HRD Corp?'; 'Panduan Program 2026' (named document). Fail: 'Executive MBA 6 Bulan Untuk Pengurus Yang Bekerja.'; 'Yuran & biasiswa'; 'Pilih kohort anda!'. (Evidence: DBP Khidmat Nasihat k=huruf besar tajuk — title examples without terminal punctuation, 'Pujangga yang Malang')

missingRules.topic: Programme name, credential names and CMI terms mid-sentence
missingRules.rule: English identifiers sit inside BM syntax as uninflected proper nouns. (1) Running name: 'program Future Ready Executive MBA' (BM classifier 'program' before the English proper noun; roman type; no italics, quotes or 'the'); BM head-first grammar applies to everything attached to it: 'kohort Future Ready Executive MBA', 'yuran program Future Ready Executive MBA', 'peserta program'. (2) The certificate wording 'Executive MBA on Future Ready Business Leadership' appears once per page inside a BM frame that marks it as a title — 'sijil bertajuk Executive MBA on Future Ready Business Leadership' or 'program Executive MBA on Future Ready Business Leadership (Executive MBA dalam Kepimpinan Perniagaan Sedia Masa Hadapan)' — so the English 'on' is read as part of a title, never as a preposition of the BM sentence; later mentions 'program ini' or the short name. (3) Never a half-translation ('Executive MBA dalam Future Ready …', 'MBA Eksekutif'), never 'sebuah' / 'satu' before the name, never a plural or possessive on the English ('Certificates', 'CMI's'), no coined acronyms ('FREMBA'); 'EMBA' only where the EN copy already uses it. (4) Do not double the classifier and the English head: not 'sijil CMI Certificate of Recognition' but 'menerima CMI Certificate of Recognition (sijil pengiktirafan CMI)' on first mention, then 'sijil pengiktirafan CMI' / 'sijil ini'. (5) 'CMI' expands once per page as 'Chartered Management Institute (CMI), United Kingdom' — English name, because it is a UK body (Do 4 covers Malaysian bodies only). (6) 'Chartered Manager' is a status: frame it with 'status' / 'laluan' / 'menjadi' — 'status Chartered Manager (CMgr)', 'laluan Chartered Manager yang berasingan dan tidak wajib, ditentukan oleh CMI' (sibling 6.4; never 'laluan pilihan'), 'menjadi Foundation Chartered Manager (fCMgr)'; the post-nominal 'fCMgr' follows a person's name. (7) 'CMI Professional Standards' stays English with the gloss 'piawaian profesional CMI' once. (8) Prepositions attach to the BM head noun, never left in English: 'untuk program Executive MBA …', 'dalam laluan Chartered Manager'. (9) Every CMI sentence names CMI as the decider ('ditentukan oleh CMI'). (10) The name is never hyphenated across a line break. Fail: `Executive MBA (dalam|untuk|bagi) (?!Kepimpinan Perniagaan Sedia Masa Hadapan\))`; `\bsijil CMI Certificate\b`; `\b(sebuah|satu) (Executive|Future Ready|CMI)`; `CMI's`; `Certificates of Recognition`; `\bFREMBA\b`; `\blaluan pilihan\b`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Peserta yang menamatkan program Future Ready Executive MBA menerima CMI Certificate of Recognition (sijil pengiktirafan CMI) daripada Chartered Management Institute (CMI), United Kingdom — sijil bertajuk Executive MBA on Future Ready Business Leadership, dianugerahkan dan disokong oleh CMI. Ini bukan ijazah akademik yang diakreditasi oleh MQA.' Fail: 'Peserta menerima sijil CMI Certificate of Recognition daripada CMI's.'; 'sebuah Executive MBA dalam Future Ready Business Leadership'; 'laluan pilihan Chartered Manager'.

missingRules.topic: Owner pattern: local term (English) for messaging vocabulary, and its precedence
missingRules.rule: Applies to concepts the owner names, not to identifiers (the previous rule runs the other way). Form: lowercase Malay term, one space, English in round brackets, roman type, no quotes, no italics, no capital on the English unless it is a proper name: 'kepimpinan berkhidmat (servant leadership)', 'kemajuan (progress)', 'harapan (hope)', 'tugas sebenar yang perlu diselesaikan (the right job to be done)', 'perkara yang betul, bukan sekadar perkara yang baik' (no gloss needed). Once per page, at the first body occurrence; if the first occurrence is a heading, gloss in the heading only when the heading stays at or under eight words, otherwise gloss in the first body sentence. After the gloss the Malay stands alone; never re-gloss, never reverse the order, never gloss inside a CTA or a table cell, never inflect the English. Precedence: where the owner file and the sibling audit differ, the owner wins — (a) 'kepimpinan berkhidmat', not 'kepimpinan yang berkhidmat'; Malay-first, not 'servant leadership (kepimpinan …)'; DBP Istilah's 'kepemimpinan kebaktian' is not used; (b) 'tugas sebenar yang perlu diselesaikan (the right job to be done)' in prose, while the curriculum label 'Jobs-To-Be-Done (JTBD)' keeps its identifier form under the previous rule and is glossed with the owner phrase on first mention; never 'kerja yang betul'; (c) the five S keep the English labels once, glossed exactly 'Kelangsungan, Keselamatan, Sosial, Kejayaan, Khidmat' — not 'penerimaan sosial', not 'kemandirian', not lowercase, and 'Kejayaan' only as that capitalised label ('berjaya'/'kejayaan' stay banned in prose, sibling 7.11); no verb ladders ('bertahan, selamat, diterima, berjaya, berkhidmat'); (d) 'kemajuan (progress)' and 'harapan (hope)' never attached to a career, salary or promised outcome; (e) 'perubahan pengalaman' stays banned (owner and sibling agree) — express it as what the reader does or sees differently ('cara anda membuat keputusan berubah'). Fail: `\(servant leadership\)` more than once per page; `servant leadership \(kepimpinan`; `\bkepimpinan yang berkhidmat\b`; `\bkepemimpinan kebaktian\b`; `\bJTBD\b` on a page without the owner gloss; `\bkerja yang betul\b`; `\bpenerimaan sosial\b|\bkemandirian\b` in the five-S gloss; `\bperubahan pengalaman\b`.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Modul ini berpaksikan kepimpinan berkhidmat (servant leadership): pemimpin yang mengutamakan keperluan pasukannya.' then 'kepimpinan berkhidmat' alone for the rest of the page; 'Lima peringkat keperluan pemimpin — Survival, Safety, Social, Success, Service (Kelangsungan, Keselamatan, Sosial, Kejayaan, Khidmat).' Fail: 'servant leadership (kepimpinan yang berkhidmat)'; a second '(servant leadership)' lower on the page; 'Kepimpinan Berkhidmat (Servant Leadership)' inside a CTA; 'Success (penerimaan … )'. (Evidence: owner-vocabulary-rules.md; https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1.aspx?keyword=servant+leadership&d=371752)

missingRules.rule: 'pengambilan' = the intake window ('pengambilan Oktober 2026', 'tarikh pengambilan'); 'kohort' = the dated group ('Kohort 17', 'kohort Oktober'); 'sesi' = one of the three weekend training sessions only. Never 'sesi pengambilan' on this site. Availability words come from the seats field (sibling rule), never typed.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Pengambilan Oktober 2026: Kohort 17 menyelesaikan 6 hari latihan dalam 3 sesi hujung minggu.' Fail: 'Sesi pengambilan Oktober' next to '3 sesi'.

missingRules.rule: No comma before 'dan' in a list ('pengurus kanan, pengarah dan pemilik perniagaan'). Roles are lower case in running text ('pengurus kanan', 'pemilik perniagaan', 'pasukan program') and capitalised only as a title after a name ('Encik Ali, Pengurus Besar'); institutional names keep their capitals ('Pasukan Program Future Ready Executive MBA' in a signature only). Fail: `, dan\b`; `\b(Pengurus Kanan|Pemilik Perniagaan|Pengarah)\b` mid-sentence without a preceding name.
missingRules.example: Pass: 'Program ini untuk pemilik perniagaan, pengarah dan pengurus kanan.'; 'Puan Farah, Pengarah Operasi, Syarikat X.' Fail: 'pemilik perniagaan, pengarah, dan pengurus kanan'; 'setiap Pengurus Kanan boleh …'.
